objective: Prepare allowlisted proof context, bounded two-container protocol fixture, and name/label-guarded cleanup for later controller-authorized runtime proof.
dependencies: root controller dispatch after read-only protected-container baseline

remoteResources.cleanupGuard: exact randomized name pattern plus exact ownership label; Docker --rm on runner exit

acceptance: Context includes only Dockerfile, compiled sandbox entrypoint, and identity metadata; frozen hashes match.
Two runsc containers coexist and Docker inspect proves user, network, rootfs, mounts, capabilities, no-new-privileges, and resource limits.
Both lanes pass init/read/replace/run_check/snapshot with unique data and snapshot hash verification.
Traversal and symlink inputs reject; oversized output is bounded; timeout terminates; exact containers disappear.
Protected container identity/start time/restart count and OAuth status are unchanged, captured read-only by controller.
Evidence explicitly limits claim to a two-container protocol fixture, not provider proof or six-lane capacity.

validationPreparation.shellSyntax: PASS; Git Bash bash -n plus both scripts return usage exit 2 without side effects

reviewFindingsAddressed: Protocol response reader now uses selector-driven incremental reads under a deadline, so partial lines cannot block.
Protocol frame cap is 16,000,000 bytes and separate from the 64,000-byte check-output assertion.
Proof image tag is inspected once and containers are created with the immutable image ID.
All Docker CLI calls use /usr/bin/docker, the explicit local socket, an initially empty private config directory, and a sanitized environment.
Runner cleanup validates exact container IDs, exact names, and all provenance labels; standalone cleanup requires the same hashes and IDs.
Runner captures codex-universal ID, StartedAt, RestartCount, and status before and after, failing on change.
The build context contains exactly the Dockerfile and compiled sandbox entry; identity metadata stays outside the context.
